**This comment is superseded. It is not the verdict of this review.** A later comment on the same head gives the verdict: needs-rework. The label edit at 04:32:06Z stands. Do not merge on this comment.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**Build route:** a local worktree at this head (the 2026-11-15 local-build order; no pr-test run). The trial merge with `origin/main` is clean. Merged head: 0a2dd7bc2.

**Test results:**
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green. 174 test binaries, 1514 passed, 0 failed, 13.9 min wall (fresh worktree build).
- New suite `sodick_alc400g`: 4 passed. `machine`: 33. `machine_library`: 11. `axis_direction`: 12. `conformance`: 7. `sodick_wire_post`: 9.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Checks:**
- The `.mch` parses (`parse_mch` in the new tests). The registration follows the Doosan rows in `posting::MACHINES`. It is the first `wire_edm` entry in the built-in library; the `draft.rs` X/Y/U/V draft and the `WIRE_POSTS` offer are pre-existing code.
- The pinned picker list in `crates/app/tests/machine.rs` gains the row, and its `MACHINES.len()` test passes. The `WireEdm` arm in that test matches the declared-kind law (`assets/machines/AGENTS.md`): axes infer a mill, never a wire EDM.
- The figures match Sodick's published datasheet: X/Y/Z 400 x 300 x 250 mm, U/V 150 x 150 mm, taper ±25 deg at 130 mm (the ALC400G PDF at sodick.formationcraft.co.uk and the product page at sales.sodick.com, read 2026-11-15). Z is left out on purpose: the wire model carries the guides as the head, not a Z part.
- Each stated travel band spans the published length (X ±200, Y ±150, U/V ±75). `machine/wire_edm.rs` judges moves and taper poses against these bands. The choice follows the lathe files and refuses early, never late. Note: the shipped mill files state bands twice the published length; `docs/decisions/1501-sodick-alc400g.md` records the choice. Not a blocker.
- The file sets no program units. Its `units` block states the units of its own numbers, as all 39 `.mch` files do. Posted units come from the document; the `program_units` suite passed.
- Unsourced data stays absent, never guessed: no guide heights, no AWT, no wire diameters, no conditions, no codes. The cut refuses by name until the user adds a condition row. The new test pins that refusal, and posts a punch through the Sodick post with a clearly marked test row.
- `sodick-wire.cps` is offered for the file (pre-existing behaviour for every wire machine). The post keeps its "NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL" note in each program, and the PR says the ALC400G control is not confirmed. The file names no post, as the grammar requires.
- No posted G-code path for existing machines changes: the diff adds only the data file, the list row, and tests.
- Provenance: the registration comment names the decision file, and the decision file lists the public sources. The `.mch` itself carries no `general.description` source line, unlike the two Doosan files. Optional follow-up only.
- Effort: medium fits `#1501`. No post logic changed, so no safety-floor escalation.

Requested changes: none.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d44bfb1483e895f4aff9371c493085ef19553a84 -->

**Needs rework.** This PR is not mergeable as written. One blocker below.

What I checked
- The file registers in `posting::MACHINES` and sorts with the other machine files. `MACHINES` drives the machine picker.
- The travel figures match the published Sodick datasheet for the ALC400G: X 400 mm, Y 300 mm, U 150 mm, V 150 mm. Each travel sits centred on zero. The stated reason is sound: the sources give the length, not the machine origin.
- The file sets no program units. Units come from the document.
- The file carries a provenance line. Unsourced values stay out.

Blocker: the machine-file schema has no wire plane entry
- The taper law in `crates/post/src/post/wire_align.rs` reads the wire-plane normal from the machine file. `Machine::wire_plane_normal` only matches a machine plane named `"top"` or `"taper"`.
- The file defines planes XY, UZ, WYZ, VX and WX only. So `wire_plane_normal` returns None.
- `crates/app/src/post/stream.rs` then posts an error: "Post cannot apply the taper: the active machine file states no wire plane."
- This is not new to this PR. No shipped machine file carries a wire plane, so no machine posts a wire taper today. But this PR names a taper limit of 25 degrees, and that limit cannot take effect through any path in the tree. A user who sets a taper on a wire operation gets a refusal, not the post the PR promises.

Requested change
- Make the file state what it can do. Either add the wire-plane entry this file needs, or state in the PR body and the file comment that the taper limit is data only until the wire plane lands. A taper limit that never applies is a silent wrong answer.
- The number 25 has no source. The public Sodick and SDMIC documents for the ALC400G give a maximum taper of 30 degrees plus or minus, on a solidcore wire-EDM page that also carries a 30-degree taper diagram. Confirm the figure against the vendor document and cite it.

Test results
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (6 binaries): 376 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The diff is 1,790 added lines across 137 files. 1,567 of them are three generated fixtures. The hand-written change is the machine file, its `MACHINES` entry, one doc line in `machine.rs`, and the fixtures.

Suggested follow-up, not a blocker
- `crates/post/tests/wire_wcs_streams.rs` never drives `taper_deg` non-zero. Only `sinker_wcs_align.rs` covers the taper law, on a sinker file with a `top` plane. A wire taper test on a file that carries a wire plane would close the gap.

An independent agent performed this review. The build and tests ran locally on this machine, in the reviewer's own worktree. No workflow runner was used.
Draft again: rework for the review. The taper source is checked and the wire-plane limit is stated. Pushes follow.

<!-- pr-reviewer: ef93ed0bf35a7593839b687f76ad7500d97bdc9f -->

Re-review of head ef93ed0b. This review supersedes the review of d44bfb14.

**Verdict: needs rework.** Two items block this PR. The two earlier blockers are closed.

## Earlier blockers

1. Taper range: Resolved. The Sodick Thailand product page
   (http://www.sodick.co.th/EN/EDW.php) states ±25° at a 130 mm work
   height for the ALC400G. The ±30° figure belongs to the ALC800GH and
   ALN800GH models. The decision file now cites one source per figure.
2. Tapered-cut refusal: Addressed. The machine file states the limit,
   and the PR body names issue #1800 for the missing capability. The
   new test
   `a_tapered_punch_is_refused_at_post_until_guide_heights_and_a_wire_plane_exist`
   passes and pins the refusal with a named diagnostic. The post never
   emits an unsupported taper path.

## Blockers at this head

1. The ribbon machine-mode law fails. The quick gate, on a trial merge
   with current main, is red in the ui suites:
   `every_kind_with_a_shipped_machine_has_a_mode` panics with "WireEdm
   has a shipped machine but no ribbon mode row". Issue #1195 added
   this law to main after the branch base. This PR registers the first
   shipped wire EDM built-in machine. Add a `WireEdm` row to
   `MACHINE_MODES` in `crates/ui/src/machine_modes.rs` (kind, caption,
   built-in machine name), and update the ribbon assertions that
   follow the table.
2. Clippy is red. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D
   warnings` fails at `crates/app/tests/sodick_alc400g.rs:149`:
   `clippy::err_expect` on `.err().expect(...)`. Use `expect_err`
   instead.

## Gate summary

- Trial merge with origin/main: clean, no conflicts.
- motion suites: ok (77 s).
- app suites: ok (1132 s). All five `sodick_alc400g` tests pass,
  including the new pinning test.
- ui suites: fail. The machine-mode test above failed; 813 passed,
  1 failed.
- clippy on camcraft-app: fail. The lint above.
- The diff is data, tests and docs, plus one registration row in
  `crates/app/src/posting.rs`.

## One fact for the record

The machine file text, the decision note and issue #1800 say the post
refuses a taper because the file "states no wire plane". No
wire-plane check exists in the code. The real refusals are the
guide-height check in `crates/app/src/machine/wire_edm.rs` and the
vertical-only rule in `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps`. The refusal
itself is real and correct. State the real mechanism in the file text
and in #1800, so #1800 carries a true premise.

This PR goes back to draft for these changes. Flag it ready for a
fresh review when the branch carries the WireEdm mode row and clippy
is clean.
